title: How to create a step-by-step financial checklist for new investors in the US
description: The definitive 'Order of Operations' for deploying your first paychecks.
content:
The most common paralysis for new investors isn't 'what to buy', but 'where to put it'. Should you pay off student loans first? Max out the 401(k)? Save for a house? Doing these in the wrong order can cost you thousands in taxes or missed employer matches. This guide provides the 'Financial Order of Operations' (FOO)—a logical, mathematically optimized checklist designed for US employees to build wealth efficiently from zero.

Key Takeaways

  • The Match is Priority #1: Never invest a dime elsewhere until you have captured 100% of your employer's 401(k) match. It is the only guaranteed 100% return.
  • High-Interest Debt is an Emergency: Credit cards (20%+) and private loans (8%+) are wealth destroyers. Pay them off before buying stocks.
  • The 'HSA' Secret Step: If eligible, the Health Savings Account comes before the Roth IRA for many optimizers due to its triple-tax advantage.
  • Taxable is Last: Do not open a Robinhood brokerage account until you have filled your tax-advantaged buckets (IRA/401k). Don't volunteer to pay taxes you don't have to.

Why It Matters (US Context)

This checklist is specific to the US tax code. It leverages the distinct advantages of 401(k)s, HSAs, and Roth IRAs. In other countries with simpler systems (like the UK's ISA or Australia's Super), the order is different.

The Financial Order of Operations

Follow this strictly. Do not skip steps.

Level 1: The Safety Net

  • Step 0: Deductibles Covered. Save $1,000 to $3,000 cash. Enough to cover your health insurance and car insurance deductibles.
  • Step 1: 401(k) Match. Contribute just enough to get the full match. (e.g., 5%).
  • Step 2: Toxic Debt. Kill anything with an interest rate > 7%.

Level 2: The Tax Shelter

  • Step 3: HSA. Maximize $4,300 (Single) / $8,550 (Family). Invest it; don't spend it.
  • Step 4: Roth IRA. Maximize $7,000. Tax-free growth forever.
  • Step 5: Remaining 401(k). Go back and fill the rest of the $23,500 limit if you have high income.

Level 3: The Freedom Fund

  • Step 6: Taxable Brokerage. Once tax shelters are full, spill over into a standard brokerage account. This is your liquidity for early retirement (pre-59.5).
  • Step 7: Low-Interest Debt. Mortgage paydown (optional).

Execution Tactics

  1. Audit Your Paycheck: Look at your paystub. Are you hitting the match? If not, log into your HR portal today and fix it.
  2. List Your Debts: Sort by Interest Rate (Avalanche Method). Ignore the balance size. Kill the highest rate first.
  3. Automate the Flow: Once you finish Step 2, set up an auto-transfer to your Roth IRA. When that is maxed ($583/mo), redirect that auto-transfer to your 401(k) or Taxable account.
  4. Revisit Annually: Limits change every year (COLA adjustments). In January, check the new IRS limits for 401(k) and IRA and adjust your contributions.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if I want to buy a house?

Insert a 'Step 3.5'. After getting the match and killing toxic debt, pause aggressive investing to hoard cash in a High-Yield Savings Account for the down payment.

Should I skip the HSA if I'm healthy?

No! Healthy people benefit most from HSAs because the money grows for decades untouched. It becomes a Super-IRA.

What if I have high student loans?

If rates are < 5%, treat them as Step 7. If > 6-7%, treat them as Step 2 (Toxic Debt). The math changes based on the interest rate environment.
